## Primary-Sourced Asset Register — May 2026

## 1. Sector Overview

Vietnam's electricity system has grown rapidly, with total installed capacity exceeding 80 GW by end-2024. Thermal generation—coal, natural gas, and oil—constitutes the backbone of baseload supply, accounting for roughly 55–60% of total generation despite rapid renewable expansion. The system is managed by Vietnam Electricity (EVN), the state-owned vertically integrated utility, with generation subsidiaries EVNGENCO1, EVNGENCO2, and EVNGENCO3 owning most domestic thermal capacity. PetroVietnam (PVN), through subsidiary PV Power, operates the major domestic gas fleet and is developing coal (Long Phú 1) and LNG projects. Vinacomin (TKV) owns mine-mouth coal plants in the northeast.

**PDP8 (Quy hoạch Điện VIII)**, approved May 2023 under Decision 500/QĐ-TTg, establishes the 2021–2030 power development plan with a vision to 2050. It caps coal at 30,127 MW (peaking ~2030) and mandates a full coal phase-out by 2050. LNG is designated the transitional fuel, with 22,400 MW targeted by 2030 across ~13 projects, though as of 2026 only the Nhơn Trạch 3&4 project (1,624 MW) has reached COD. The **Amended PDP8** (Decision 768/QĐ-TTg, April 2025) adjusts LNG to 22,524 MW and defers two projects (Long Sơn, Long An II) to 2031–2035.

Key challenges include: (a) severe delays in LNG projects due to PPA framework gaps, gas pricing uncertainty, and LNG terminal infrastructure; (b) coal phase-down commitments under the Just Energy Transition Partnership (JETP) conflicting with baseload reliability needs; (c) financing constraints as international banks exit coal; and (d) integration of ~25 GW of variable renewables (solar + wind) requiring flexible gas-fired capacity.

Foreign BOT developers play a significant role: seven coal BOT plants (Mông Dương 2, Vĩnh Tân 1, Nghi Sơn 2, Vân Phong 1, Vũng Áng 2, Hải Dương, Duyên Hải 2) are operated by Japanese, Korean, Chinese, and Malaysian consortia under 25-year PPAs with government guarantees.

## 2. Per-Plant Narratives — Major/Disputed/Ambiguous Assets

### Vĩnh Tân Complex (Bình Thuận Province)
The Vĩnh Tân Power Centre is Vietnam's largest thermal generation cluster (~4,244 MW operating). **Vĩnh Tân II** (2×622 MW, EVNGENCO3, COD 2014–15) and **Vĩnh Tân IV** (2×600 MW, EVNGENCO3, COD 2017–18) plus **Vĩnh Tân IV MR** (1×600 MW, COD 2019) use subcritical/supercritical imported coal technology. **Vĩnh Tân I** (2×600 MW, BOT, COD 2018–19) is operated by China's COPI consortium. **Vĩnh Tân III** (~1,980 MW) was cancelled after CLP Holdings withdrew from coal in 2019. The complex has been a flashpoint for environmental protests.

### Thái Bình 2
A 1,200 MW (2×600 MW) supercritical coal plant developed by PVN/PV Power in Thái Bình province. The project experienced massive delays and cost overruns, becoming a subject of anti-corruption investigations. Unit 1 achieved COD in mid-2022 and Unit 2 in early 2023. Original EPC by LILAMA/PVC.

### Ô Môn LNG Complex (Cần Thơ)
Ô Môn I (660 MW, CCGT, EVNGENCO2) is the only operating unit, fuelled by depleting Cửu Long Basin gas. Ô Môn II (~1,050 MW), III (~1,050 MW), and IV (~1,050 MW) are planned to use Block B (Lô B) gas from the offshore Ô Môn gas pipeline. Development is contingent on the Block B upstream project reaching FID. PDP8 lists all three for completion by 2030, but none has commenced construction.

### Sơn Mỹ LNG (Bình Thuận Province)
Two LNG-to-power plants (~2,250 MW each, total ~4,500 MW) planned alongside the Sơn Mỹ LNG terminal. The terminal is being developed by a consortium including AES and PetroVietnam Gas. The power plants lack confirmed developers. PDP8 lists them for 2027–2030 but progress has been minimal.

### Nhơn Trạch 3 & 4 (Đồng Nai Province)
Vietnam's first LNG-to-power project to reach COD. Developed by PV Power, 2×812 MW (total 1,624 MW) CCGT using Mitsubishi M701JAC gas turbines. LNG supplied via Thị Vải terminal. COD achieved 2025. This project serves as the PPA/regulatory template for subsequent LNG plants.
